runners_data.name: Clover Time
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with consistent 5f form who should track Coast ideally, though 30 days off the track raises slight fitness questions

runners_data.name: Cabeza De Llave
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs pace to aim at but has shown ability at this trip, with 63 days absence a concern for sharpness

runners_data.name: Irish Dancer
runners_data.note: Another prominent type fresh from a recent run, capable of stalking Coast but trainer form remains poor at 0/14

runners_data.name: Sonic Si
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with decent recent form who may struggle if Coast sets modest fractions, but trainer hitting 20% strike rate recently

runners_data.name: Brian The Snail
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse wearing cheekpieces who needs a strong pace to be effective, age 12 a significant concern

runners_data.name: Man On A Mission

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner carrying bottom weight who should get uncontested lead, but poor recent form and 45-day break raise stamina doubts

races.paceDynamic: Coast will be the sole early leader in this small field, setting what should be a steady tempo over 5f with no immediate pressure. Clover Time and Irish Dancer are the only prominent runners but both can settle just behind rather than challenge early. The majority of the field - Cabeza De Llave, Sonic Si, Brian The Snail, and Man On A Mission - are all hold-up horses who will need the race to come to them. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent horses, as Coast gets an uncontested lead while the hold-up brigade may find limited room for manoeuvre in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coast Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Coast gets an easy lead and maintains stamina over 5f
scenarios.body: The veteran sets sustainable fractions and kicks clear in the final furlong, while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground. Front-runners and prominent racers dominate as the pace becomes solid but not punishing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Clover Time or Irish Dancer track Coast closely and outstay him
scenarios.body: The prominent pair use their tactical advantage to strike in the final 2f as Coast weakens, benefiting from the honest gallop. Hold-up horses still find themselves with too much to do despite Coast's fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If Coast goes too fast early or weakens dramatically
scenarios.body: The pace becomes genuinely strong allowing one of the closers to pick up the pieces late. Man On A Mission or Cabeza De Llave capitalize on their light weights and fitness edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Coast stops quickly and the prominent runners also struggle
scenarios.body: The race becomes a scramble with no clear pace advantage, allowing any runner with a turn of foot to capitalize. Form and class become more important than running style.

watchPoints.text: Coast's stamina reserves after 45 days off - if he stops in the final furlong, it opens the race completely
How aggressively Clover Time and Irish Dancer track Coast early - sitting too far back could be fatal in this tactical setup
Man On A Mission's position turning for home - needs to be within 3-4 lengths to have any chance from his hold-up style
The pace through the first 2f - if Coast goes too conservatively, the hold-up horses have no pace to aim at
Brian The Snail's response to the cheekpieces at age 12 - needs career-best effort to feature from unfavourable race shape

races.paceDynamic: Rose Warrior stands out as the sole confirmed front runner in this field of predominantly hold-up horses, giving him an uncontested lead over the extended 1m6f trip. With ten runners adopting waiting tactics behind him, Rose Warrior can dictate a comfortable gallop without early pressure, setting up a sustainable pace that will suit his stamina-laden profile. The lack of pace competition means the race will likely develop into a sprint finish from the back, but Rose Warrior's ability to control the tempo gives front runners and prominent racers a significant tactical advantage. This race shape strongly favours early pace horses who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rose Warrior Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Warrior gets an uncontested lead and sustains his gallop
scenarios.body: He dictates ideal fractions without pressure and kicks clear when the hold-up horses are still finding their stride. The 193-day break becomes irrelevant as his stamina and tactical position prove decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and Rose Warrior stops in the straight
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get their preferred scenario with a sprint finish, allowing the classier performers to unleash their turn of foot. Traffic becomes crucial as ten horses converge late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Modest Gallop Suits
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Warrior sets a steady tempo but gets caught close home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of who can quicken best from the pack, favouring horses with recent winning form and good turn of foot. Positioning in the straight becomes vital.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Warrior goes too fast early or stops completely
scenarios.body: The race falls apart tactically with horses coming from everywhere, creating a messy finish where the best-positioned horse wins. Jockey skill becomes paramount in the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Rose Warrior's jumping from the stalls - if he misses the break his entire tactical advantage disappears
Traffic problems in the straight as ten hold-up horses converge simultaneously from the back of the field
Abila's early positioning with De Sousa - needs to be closer than usual given his class advantage
The pace in the middle stages - if Rose Warrior goes too slow he becomes a sitting duck
Hickton and Angelardo as the only recent winners - their confidence could prove decisive in a tight finish

races.paceDynamic: Temple will take them along at a sustainable gallop from the front with no early pressure in this small field of eight. The prominent runner faces minimal pace pressure early, allowing him to dictate terms through steady sectionals over this 1m4f trip. With six hold-up horses including the classy Chasing Time, Kenneth, and Birgham Dub all needing to be delivered late, Temple's uncontested lead creates a tactical scenario where he can kick clear before the closers get organised. This race shape strongly favours the pace-setter Temple, as the hold-up brigade may find themselves with too much ground to make up if he gets first run in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Temple steals it
scenarios.trigger: If Temple gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear at the right moment
scenarios.body: The front-runner exploits the lack of early pace pressure to build an unassailable advantage before the hold-up horses can mount their challenges. His 7lb claimer Moldoveanu times the acceleration perfectly as the closers struggle to peg back the deficit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class tells late
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses time their runs perfectly and Temple's stamina cracks
scenarios.body: Kenneth and Chasing Time use their superior class ratings to reel in Temple's advantage in the final furlong. The Gosden and Appleby strings have the tactical nous to overcome the unfavourable pace scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise closer strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the other hold-up horses produces an unexpected turn of foot
scenarios.body: Ramli or Birgham Dub capitalises on the focus being on the main protagonists to sneak through and win at bigger odds. Their fresher profiles compared to the long-absent Kenneth give them an edge in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If Temple stops quickly and sets up a cavalry charge finish
scenarios.body: The front-runner's lack of recent racing tells as multiple hold-up horses converge in a bunch finish. This creates chaos where any of the closers could prevail in a tight photo finish.

watchPoints.text: Temple could steal this if he gets an easy lead and kicks at the right moment before the closers react
Kenneth's 378-day layoff is massive even for the Gosden yard and could blunt his finishing kick
Multiple hold-up horses could get in each other's way if Temple doesn't go clear early enough
Chasing Time has the best recent AW form but needs pace pressure early to set up his late run
The 7lb claims on Temple and Ramli could prove decisive in a tight finish

Rock Iguana and Selection may track him prominently but neither is aggressive enough to challenge for the lead early. This sets up a controlled gallop that will suit the patient hold-up performers who can unleash late kicks. The sustainable pace favours hold-up horses who can close strongly in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Bell Shot sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays moderate throughout
scenarios.body: The patient closers get ideal racing room and timing to unleash their finishing kicks. Hold-up horses with proven closing ability dominate the finish as the early pace proves too soft.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Bell Shot Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Bell Shot finds more than expected and maintains his lead under pressure
scenarios.body: The front runner capitalizes on his uncontested position and holds off late challengers. His recent form at this trip and lack of early pressure gives him every chance to stay strong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Battle

scenarios.label: D

races.paceDynamic: Zambezi Diamond is the sole confirmed front runner in this 13-runner maiden fillies' field and should get an uncontested lead, though her tendency to fade late creates vulnerability. The prominent runners Zarinca, Positive Thoughts, and Sandy Craic will likely settle just behind, while the hold-up horses Luna Celeste, Dreamadera, and The Wind And Sun will be tracking from midfield and rear positions. With only one pace-setter who has finishing concerns, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and those with strong finishing kicks who can exploit the likely collapse of the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Zambezi Diamond sets honest fractions but fades as expected in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade gets the perfect setup with Luna Celeste and Highland Bear able to unleash late runs. This plays directly into their preferred tactical approach with plenty of pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Capitalize
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group can position perfectly behind the fading leader without going too hard early
scenarios.body: Zarinca and Sandy Craic are best placed to inherit when Zambezi Diamond weakens, having the tactical speed to kick clear. Their running styles are ideal for this mid-race positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Zambezi Diamond gets very soft sectionals and conserves enough energy for a sustained finish
scenarios.body: Despite her fading tendencies, the mare could exploit the tactical race by dictating terms completely. Her experience advantage over these maidens becomes crucial in a slowly-run affair.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantities Strike
scenarios.trigger: If any of the three lightly-raced debutants Rumble Ruby, Rianka, or Whazzimo show significant improvement
scenarios.body: The newcomers could have been working better than their odds suggest and benefit from the strong pace setup. Their unknown ratings suggest potential upside that the market hasn't recognized.

The three debutants Rumble Ruby, Rianka, and Whazzimo are completely unknown quantities who could surprise

races.paceDynamic: Safe Harbor will set the pace from the front with no pressure from the other four hold-up horses. This creates a comfortable tempo where Safe Harbor can dictate fractions without being challenged early. The lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a sprint from 2f out when the hold-up brigade make their moves. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the traffic problems that will inevitably occur when four hold-up horses all come with late runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Safe Harbor gets soft fractions and maintains stamina
scenarios.body: The front-runner controls every call and has enough left to resist late challengers who face traffic problems in a bunch finish. Safe Harbor's prominent style becomes the winning move when others are still organising their runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Safe Harbor weakens in final furlong and traffic clears
scenarios.body: The four hold-up horses get clear runs simultaneously and produce a cavalry charge finish with the best staying power prevailing. My Champion and What Fools Believe have shown the strongest recent form to capitalise.

scenarios.label: C

scenarios.body: Multiple runners get hampered when making their moves, creating a messy finish where only those with clear passages can win. The jockeys' experience becomes crucial in finding daylight.

scenarios.label: D

scenarios.trigger: If Kalokalo's 203-day break proves beneficial rather than rusty
scenarios.body: The longest absence runner comes back refreshed and benefits from the tactical chaos, with Saffie Osborne finding a smooth passage through the field. Charles Hills' strike rate suggests confidence in the comeback.

My Champion's visor and claiming jockey combination creating extra urgency in finish

races.paceDynamic: Iconic Times will take them along from the front with no other natural pace-setters in this 11-runner field. Give Me The Night may track prominently but the overall gallop will be steady and controlled. With 9 of the 11 runners holding up horses, including strong finishers like Marry The Night and King Of York, this sets up as a typical all-weather sprint finish from the back. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finish, as they'll get the perfect scenario of a modest pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Iconic Times sets modest fractions and the field bunches entering the straight
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up brigade gets the perfect setup with plenty to aim at in the final two furlongs. King Of York, Marry The Night and Soames Forsyte all have the class and finishing kick to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Give Me The Night can secure the perfect tracking position behind Iconic Times
scenarios.body: The prominent runner avoids the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the back-markers in a bunched finish. Give Me The Night gets first run on the field while the hold-up horses are still fighting for racing room.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Iconic Times goes too slowly and creates a stop-start gallop that favours nothing
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with horses bumping into the back of each other and no clear pace bias emerging. Any horse with luck in running can prevail regardless of typical running style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Bolts
scenarios.trigger: If Iconic Times gets competitive and sets a genuine gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The early leader maintains momentum and the hold-up horses find the sustained pace too demanding to reel in. Iconic Times exploits the lack of early pressure to control the race from wire to wire.

watchPoints.text: Iconic Times must be watched for how genuine the early gallop is - if too slow it creates chaos

Goldie Trickett's fitness after 180 days off warrants monitoring despite the quality jockey booking
